chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Sa'id ibn Yasar from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever dies and has not performed the Hajj of Islam, and left nothing except enough for the cost of Hajj, then his heirs have more right to what he left; if they wish, they perform Hajj on his behalf, and if they wish, they consume it.

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory pilgrimage to Mecca

ai.seo_question: What happens to the estate of a deceased person who hasn't performed Hajj and has limited funds?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies the priority of debt and estate distribution over the fulfillment of the obligatory Hajj when resources are limited, a key principle in Shia fiqh. It highlights the heirs' discretion (ikhtiyar) in balancing the spiritual obligation of Hajj al-Islam against their own financial rights, reflecting the juristic balance between individual piety and familial welfare.
